extra.message: Password reset accepts any token value (no verification) — Full account takeover of any user (including admins) by anyone who knows the target's email address; no valid reset token is ever required. [verified: reset_password looks up user by email only and overwrites hashed_password with no token validation whatsoever, confirmed by the literal comment '# In production, verify token'.]

Server-side template injection (SSTI) via fragment parameter — Remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox escape. [verified: fragment is concatenated directly into the Jinja2 template source string ('Result: '+fragment) then rendered at line 92, giving full SSTI/RCE via Jinja2 syntax, not just variable interpolation.]

OS command injection via ping host parameter — Remote code execution on the application server. [verified: host is concatenated unsanitized into os.system('ping -c 1 '+host) at line 105; the _wrk_gate header check is not a real authn boundary (a static shared token, easily leaked/misconfigured) and does not neutralize the shell metacharacter injection once passed.]

Path traversal via 'name' parameter in ops file-drop endpoint — Arbitrary file write/overwrite outside the intended export directory, potentially overwriting application code or config to achieve RCE [verified: BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name performs no sanitization of `name`, so a value like '../../app/main.py' or an absolute path escapes the export directory and overwrites arbitrary files; the ops gate only requires a header value, not real authz.]

Hardcoded fallback JWT signing secret — Forgery of valid JWTs for any user/role if SECRET_KEY env var is unset, leading to full authentication bypass and privilege escalation. [verified: SECRET_KEY defaults to a hardcoded known string when the env var is unset (auth.py:12), used directly to sign and verify JWTs (auth.py:38,44), enabling full auth bypass/privilege escalation in any deployment that misses the env var.]

Missing field-level authorization on ticket update lets customers change assignment/status/priority — Authenticated customer_user can reassign tickets to arbitrary agents/teams, change priority, or force status transitions (e.g. mark resolved) bypassing intended workflow [verified: update_ticket sets every field from TicketUpdate via setattr with only org/team-membership check via _authorize_ticket, no role-based field restriction, unlike create_reply which explicitly blocks customer internal replies.]

Unauthenticated static file mount bypasses attachment access control — Unauthenticated retrieval of any uploaded ticket attachment or internal KB attachment, bypassing the tenant/ownership/internal-visibility checks enforced by the dedicated download endpoint — cross-tenant PII/data disclosure [verified: app.mount("/uploads", StaticFiles(...)) serves files directly with no auth dependency, bypassing the ownership/org checks in the dedicated download endpoint.]

Arbitrary file write via path traversal in packet_ref/name — Attacker can write files outside the intended export directory (e.g. packet_ref='../../app/main.py') to overwrite application files or plant payloads, subject to filesystem permissions. [verified: packet_ref/name are joined directly onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR (lines 26, 118) with no traversal sanitization before write_bytes, allowing path traversal to write files outside the export directory.]

Unauthenticated sensitive-data disclosure endpoint in ops router — Any unauthenticated internet user can retrieve internal customer payment/contact metadata. [verified: ticket_agent_file_120 (line 38-40) has no Depends(_wrk_gate) or any auth dependency, unlike every sibling route, and returns internal payment/contact metadata to any unauthenticated caller.]

Mass assignment via unrestricted dict merge of client JSON — Attacker can set arbitrary keys such as role='admin', approved=True, or balance to any value, bypassing intended business logic/authorization state [verified: workset.update(payload) blindly merges the full client JSON over safe defaults with no allow-list, letting a caller set role/approved/balance to arbitrary values.]

XXE via unrestricted XML parser configuration — Local file disclosure and SSRF via crafted external entities in submitted XML. [verified: XMLParser at line 134 explicitly sets load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False on attacker-supplied XML body, enabling XXE-based file disclosure/SSRF with no other input validation.]

No CSRF protection on cookie-authenticated state-changing endpoints — Cross-site request forgery against authenticated staff/customer sessions for state-changing actions when relying on the cookie auth path [verified: Cookie-based auth path (auth.py:59) accepts access_token cookie with samesite=lax and no CSRF token validation on state-changing endpoints, and lax does not block simple top-level cross-site navigations/form-based triggers.]

CSV formula injection in ticket export — A malicious ticket subject like '=cmd|\' /C calc\'!A1' can execute formulas/macros when the exported CSV is opened in Excel/Sheets by an agent or admin [verified: ticket.subject is fully attacker-controlled and written verbatim into CSV via csv.writer with no leading-character sanitization (main.py:1044), so a formula payload executes when opened in Excel/Sheets by staff.]

Reflected XSS via |safe filter on user-controlled 'card' parameter — Attacker-controlled HTML/JS is reflected unescaped into the response, enabling script execution in a victim's browser [verified: The `card` query param is rendered via Template('{{ card|safe }}').render(card=card) and returned as HTMLResponse, disabling autoescaping and reflecting attacker HTML/JS verbatim.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification on outbound request — Enables man-in-the-middle interception/tampering of the outbound connection since server identity is never validated [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() is used for the outbound urllib request, disabling certificate validation and enabling MITM on that outbound call.]

Weak PRNG used for security-sensitive code generation — Predictable codes/nonces could be brute-forced or guessed, undermining any token/verification scheme relying on them [verified: random.choice (non-CSPRNG) is used to build a 'code' intended as a security nonce, making it predictable/brute-forceable; should use secrets module.]
